rounds.text: Vertoz Ltd presents a compelling case of a business whose fundamental growth has significantly outpaced its market valuation. The company has demonstrated robust long-term performance, with compounded sales growth reaching 38% over the last decade and 52% over the last three years [E14, E16]. This operational success is further evidenced by a strong cash conversion ratio of 2.31x, confirming that reported profits are effectively backed by cash [E33]. Despite this, the stock trades at a modest P/E of 12.9x, which is notably lower than the sector benchmark of 17.71x [E1, E6]. The disconnect between the company's 26% CAGR profit growth over the last five years and the -6% share price growth over the same period suggests that the market has failed to price in the underlying business expansion [E59, E22, E56]. Furthermore, the significant increase in promoter holdings from 48.96% to 64.80% signals strong internal confidence in the company's future [E41]. Conceded: the stock has suffered a 50.2% decline over the last twelve months, and 63% of promoter holdings are currently pledged [E52, E62].
